ideas.title: Northgate Container Terminal will charge a congestion fee on export containers that arrive
ideas.text: Northgate Container Terminal will charge a congestion fee on export containers that arrive more than five days before the vessel's cut-off, starting 1 December. The terminal says its yard has been more than 85 percent full for three weeks because shippers are sending boxes early to beat the year-end rush. The fee is charged per container per day after the free period and is billed to the shipping line, which usually passes it on to the shipper. Exporters should check the cut-off date on their booking and plan trucking so the container reaches the terminal inside the free window. Several lines that call at the terminal are expected to publish their own notices this week. In the comments, members say some boxes were already stored for seven days in November.

ideas.title: New HS code notes for wooden furniture parts take effect next month
ideas.text: New HS code notes for wooden furniture parts take effect on 1 December. Under the notes, flat-pack parts shipped separately from the finished furniture (legs, frames, panels) are classified under the heading for furniture parts, not under the heading for worked wood. The duty rate in most destination markets is the same, but the change affects certificates of origin, because the product description must match the new heading. Exporters who ship parts on their own should update the HS code in their commercial invoice, packing list and certificate application before the first December shipment. The three photos below show the examples given in the customs notice: a table leg, a cabinet frame and a drawer panel. Ask your customs broker to confirm the code for each item if your parts differ from these examples.

ideas.title: Spot rates for containers from Southeast Asia to the US West Coast eased for the second we
ideas.text: Spot rates for containers from Southeast Asia to the US West Coast eased for the second week in a row, according to three forwarders we spoke to. Shipping lines added capacity after the peak season and some sailings left with space to spare. Rates for 40-foot containers are now lower than in October, but carriers have announced a general rate increase for 1 December that may reverse part of the fall. Shippers with cargo ready in late November may want to book before the increase. Long-term contracts are not affected. Forwarders advise asking for a quote that states clearly which surcharges are included.

ideas.text: The access road to the river port's container yard will close from Saturday 22:00 to Sunday 18:00 for resurfacing. Trucks will be sent to a detour that adds about 40 minutes each way. ideas.title: How a container booking really works
ideas.text: Today we follow one container from booking to loading. First the shipper or the forwarder asks the shipping line for space on a sailing and gets a booking confirmation with a booking number. That confirmation lists the vessel, the voyage, the port of loading and the cut-off times. The empty container is picked up from the depot with a release order, then loaded at the factory and sealed. The truck must bring the full container to the terminal before the container-yard cut-off, and the shipping instructions must reach the line before the document cut-off, or the box can miss the vessel. After loading, the line issues the bill of lading. Most delays we see come from late trucks and late shipping instructions, not from the ship. So the one habit that saves the most money is to write the cut-off dates on your production plan the day you get the booking.

ideas.title: Exporters must issue an e-invoice for every export shipment from 1 January
ideas.text: From 1 January, every export shipment must be covered by an electronic invoice issued before the goods are declared to customs, according to a new notice from the national tax office. The rule applies to all exporters, including small businesses that still issue paper invoices for export sales. The e-invoice number must be entered on the customs declaration; declarations without it will be returned for correction. The tax office says exporters can use any approved e-invoice provider and that the change aims to speed up VAT refunds for exporters. Businesses that already use e-invoices for domestic sales only need to switch on the export invoice type with their provider. The notice gives a three-month transition period during which declarations with a missing number will be accepted with a warning. Exporters should check their invoicing software before the end of December.

ideas.title: Freight rates to Northern Europe climb for a third week
ideas.text: Container freight rates from Asia to Northern Europe rose for the third week in a row, as shipping lines cut sailings to match lower demand after the peak season. A 40-foot container now costs about 12 percent more than at the start of November on the main routes, according to a weekly rate index. Lines have also announced an emergency bunker surcharge from 1 December. Analysts expect rates to stay firm until the Lunar New Year rush in January. Exporters with cargo for Europe in December should confirm space early and ask whether quotes include the new surcharge. Contract rates signed earlier in the year are not affected unless the contract allows surcharges to be passed on.

ideas.title: The river port now lets trucking companies book a gate appointment online, up to three day
ideas.text: The river port now lets trucking companies book a gate appointment online, up to three days ahead. Drivers with an appointment use a separate lane and skip the general queue. The port says appointments are free during a two-month trial, and slots open every 30 minutes from 06:00 to 22:00. Trucking companies need an account on the port's portal and the container number for each booking. Exporters should ask their trucker whether they have signed up, because unbooked trucks will wait longer during busy hours. The port plans to make appointments compulsory for export deliveries next year.

oa_article.title: From booking to loading: the two cut-offs that matter
oa_article.body:
Every booking confirmation lists the vessel, the voyage and two deadlines.

The container-yard cut-off is the last moment the full container can enter the terminal. The document cut-off is the last moment the shipping instructions can reach the line.

Missing either can mean missing the vessel. Most delays come from late trucks and late documents, not from the ship.

What to do: write both cut-off dates into your production plan as soon as the booking is confirmed.

Source: Freight Explained, 14/11/2026
